details.body: Yacht, s. kelipotaH, krIqAnO f.
YACHT: kelipotaH: v. Boat.
YACHT , s. krIqAnOkA, krIqAnOH f., kelinOkA, kelinOH f.
Yak, s. camaraH (rI f.)
YAK: camara (f. rI), a fan made of y.'s tail (an ensign of royalty): cAmaram.
Yam, s. Alu(ru)kaM.
YAM: Alu (ru) kam, Bha. Note the following species: (1) raktAlukam;(2) kAzWAlukam;(3) SfNgAlukam;(4) piRqAlukam;(5) hastyAlukam;(6) saptAlukam.
YAM , s. AluH -lu m. n., AlakaM, maDumUlaM, maDvAlukaM, sukandaH, KaRqa- kAluH -lukaM, KaRqakarRaH.

YAMA , s. (God of Naraka or Hell, Regent of the South, or lower world, and judge of departed souls, corresponding to the grecian god Pluto, or to the judge of hell, Minos. His abode is in the infernal city of Yamapur, whither the Hindūs believe that a departed soul imme- diately repairs, and receiving a just sentence from Yama. [Page848-a+ 52] ascends to Swarga, the first heaven, or descends to Na- raka, the snaky hell, or assumes on earth the form of some animal, unless its offences have been such as deserve condemnation to a vegetable or even to a mineral prison. As god of justice and lord of punish- ment, Yama corresponds with Śiva and Varuna, and in this character is represented as bearing a cord or noose. Yama is often identified with Death and Time. He is the son of Surya or the Sun, and brother of the per- sonified Yamuna or Jumnā river) yamaH, yamarAjaH, yamarAw m. (j), yamanaH, SamanaH. — (As Death or Time or the Destroyer) kftAntaH, mftyuH m., kAlaH, kAlAntakaH, antakaH, kAlakuRWaH. — (Regent of the South) dakziRASApatiH m. — (Lord of the dead) pretapa- tiH m., pretarAjaH, paretarAw m. (j), paretarAjaH. — (Lord of deceased ancestors) pitfpatiH m. — (God of the śrāddha) SrAdDadevaH, SrAdDa- devatA. — (God of justice) DarmmarAjaH, DarmmaH. — (The impartial judge) samavarttI m. — (God of punishment) daRqaDaraH, daRqI m. (n), daRqayAmaH, aDidaRqanetA m. (tf), daRqaH. — (Bearer of the cord or noose) pASI m. (n), pASaBft m., pASapARiH m. — (Son of the sun) vEvasvataH, sUryyaputraH, sUryyatanayaH, arkatanayaH, arkanandanaH. — (Brother of Yamuna) yamunABrAtA m. — (The variegated one) citraH. The pain or punishment inflicted by Yama is called yAtanA. ‘One of his attendants,’ kAlapuruzaH.

YAMUNĀ , s. (A river, commonly called Jumna, which rises on the south side of the Himālayas, and after a course of 378 miles, falls into the Ganges at Prayaga or Allaha- bad. The personified river is considered to be the daughter of Surya or the Sun, and sister of Yama) yamunA, sUryyatanayA, sUryyaputrI, arkatanayA, yamasvasA f. (sf), SamanasvasA f., kAlindI.
YANKEE: of United States: *ayaNkaH.
Yard, s. aMganaM, prAMgaRaM, catvaraM, ajiraM. 2 gajaH. 3 kUpakAzWaM.
YARD: I A court: aNganam, prANgaRam;(2) catvaram; (3) ajiram (rare), Ki. i. 16.II A measure: gajaH, Li.III of a sail.: kUpa- kAzWam (?).
YARD , s. aNganaM, prANgaRaM, catvaraM, ajiraM, see COURT-YARD. — (The measure) gajaH. — (Of a ship) nOvasanakAzWaM, nOvasanadaRqaH.
Yarn, s. sUtraM, (OrRa-)sUtraM-taMtuH.
YARN: I Lit.: sUtram (general name).II Fig.: dIrGakaTA.
YARN , s. (Woollen thread) UrRAsUtraM, OrRasUtraM, OrRatantuH m., UrRA- mayasUtraM. — (Long yarn) dIrGasUtraM.
Yawl, s. nO f., tarI.
YAWL: nOviSezaH; *potakaH.
Yawn, v. i. vi-, jfMB 1 A, ja(jaM)B 1 A. [Yawn]ing, s. jfMBaH-BA, vi-, jfMBaRaM, vi-, jfMBikA-jfMBita. [Yawn]er, s. vi-jfMBakaH.
YAWN (v.): jfmBate, vi-, pra-, (jfmB, c. 1.): v. To gape.
YAWN (subs.): (1) jfmBA;(2) jfmBaRam;(3) jfmBitam, etc.
To YAWN , v. n. jfmB (c. 1. jfmBate -mBituM), vijfmB, prajfmB, jaBa or jamB (c. 1. jaBate, jamBate -mBituM), jfmBaRaM kf, jfmBaM, kf, vijfmBaRaM kf, glE (c. 1. glAyati, glAtuM). See To GAPE.
YAWN , YAWNING, s. jfmBaH -mBaRaM, jfmBA -mBikA, vijfmBaRaM, jfmBitaM, vijfmBitaM, hAPikA, harmma n. (n), upapuzpikA.
YAWNER , s. jfmBakaH, jfmBI m. (n), vijfmBakaH, jfmBaRakArI m.
YE: yUyam (pl.); yuvAm (dual).
YE , pron. yUyaM (nom. pl. (yuzmad).
Yea, adv. bAQaM, om; See Yes. 2 aparaM ca, api ca.
YEA: I In assent: vAQam: v. Yes.II More- -over, also: q. v.: taTA. Y. more: aDikaYca.
YEA , adv. vAQaM, Am, satyaM, hum, taTeti, aparaYca; ‘yea and nay,’ svIkArAsvIkArO m. du., svIkftAsvIkftaM.
YEAL: I Subs.: cItkAraH: v. Scream, cry. II Verb: utkroSatri (kruS, c. 1.): v. To scream, shout.
YEALLOW-BIRD, YELLOW-HAMMER: haridrANgaH.

Year, s. varzaH-rzaM, saM-, vatsaraH, abdaH, hAyanaH, samA f. (pl.), Sarad f., saMvat ind.; ‘12 y(ear)s old’ dvAdaSavArzika (kI f.); ‘2 y(ear)s old’ dvihAyanI (bAlA), ‘approached their 16th y(ear)’ zoqaSavarzAtmakA baBUvuH, zoqaSavarzavayovasTAmaspfSan; ‘this or current y(ear)’ vartamAnavarzaM, Ezamas ind.; ‘last y(ear)’ gatavarzaM, parut ind.; ‘the y(ear) before last’ parAri ind.; ‘next y(ear)’ uttara-AgAmi-vatsaraH; paravarzaM; ‘half-y(ear)’ zaRmAsaM, varzArDaM; ‘throughout the y(ear)’ AvarzAMtAt; ‘y(ear) after y(ear)’ prativarzaM, vatsare vatsare. [Year]ly, a. vArzika-sAMvatsarika-Abdika- (kI f.), prati°; ‘half-y(ear)’ arDavArzika-zARmAsika (kI f.). adv. varze varze, prativarzaM, pratisaMvatsaraM &c.

YEAR: (1) varzam, in three y. s.: varzatrayeRa, K.; for twelve y. s: dvAdaSavarzARi, D. vi.; became ten y. s old: baBUva daSavArzikaH, D. b. vii. 15. 44.; lasting twelve y. s: dvAdaSavArzikaH (kI, kaM), U. ii.;(2) vatsaraH, saM-, Li. 50.;(3) abdaH, in the 8th. y. from conception: garBAzwame'bde, M. ii. 36.;(4) hAyanaH, (a cow) four, three y. s old: catuztrihAyaRI, H. c. i. 4. 338.;(5) samA (mostly in pl.), 14 y. s: caturdaSa samAH, Vi. iv. 41.; for 100 y. s: sahasra- samam, B. p. 4.;(6) Sarad, (= autumn): v. Winter. Ph.: last y.: parut, A.; of last y.: parutra (f. trI) (rare); this y.: Ezamas, A.; y. before last: parAri (inde.), A.: of y. before last: parAritra (f. trI) (rare).

YEAR , s. vatsaraH, varzaH, saMvatsaraH, parivatsaraH, abdaH, samA, samAH m. (s), saMvad ind., hAyanaH, varizaM, kAlagranTiH m., ftuvfttiH f., sarvvarttuparivarttaH, mAsamAnaH, yugAMSakaH, Sarad f., SaradA; ‘half-year,’ varzArdDaM, abdArdDaM, zaRmAsaM, ayanaM; ‘last year,’ gatavarzaH, parut indec.; ‘belonging to it,’ parutnaH -tnI -tnaM; ‘the present year,’ varttamAnavarzaH, Ezamas; ‘year before last,’ parAri indec.; ‘belonging to it,’ parA- ritnaH -tnI -tnaM, ‘next year,’ paravarzaH, AgAmivatsaraH, uttaravatsaraH; ‘events of the year,’ varzaPalaM; ‘throughout the year, to the end of it,’ AvarzAntAt; ‘for a year,’ varzaparyyantaM; ‘year after year,’ varze varze, vatsare vatsare, prativatsaraM; ‘solar year,’ sOravarzaH; [Page848-b+ 52] ‘sidereal year,’ ArkzavarzaH.

YEARLY: I Adj.:(1) vArzika (f. kI);(2) vAtsarika (f. kI);(3) Abdika (f. kI);(4) prativArzika (f. kI); etc. Half-y.:(1) zARmAsika (f. kI);(2) arDavArzika (f. kI); etc.II Adv.:(1) varze varze;(2) prativarzam;(3) anu- vatsaram, etc.

YEARLY , a. vArzikaH -kI -kaM, prativArzikaH &c., sAMvatsarikaH -kI -kaM, sAMvatsaraH -rI -raM, AbdikaH -kI -kaM, pratisAMvatsarikaH &c., varzEkaH -kA -kaM, samInaH -nA -naM; ‘half-yearly,’ zARmAsikaH -kI -kaM.
YEARLY , adv. prativarzaM, prativatsaraM, pratyabdaM, anuvatsaraM, vatsare vatsare, varze varze, ayane ayane.

Yearn, v. i. spfh 10; snih 4 P; See Long; utkaMW 1 A, (utkaMWate ca yuzmatsannikarzasya U. 6), utsukAyate-vatsalAyate (D.); nUnamanapatyatA mAM vatsalayati (S. 7), ‘causes me to y(earn) towards the child’. [Yearn]ing, s. spfhA, utkaMWA, OtsukyaM, vAtsalyaM.
YEARN: (1) spfhayati (spfh, c. 10. = long for: q. v.);(2) snihyati (snih, c. 4. = to have affection for);(3) utsukAyate (nomi. = to be eager).
To YEARN , v. n. vatsala (nom. vatsalAyate), vAtsalyaM sUc (c. 10. sUca- yati -yituM), vatsakAmA BU, vatsalIBU, snih (c. 4. snihyati, snehituM), utsuka (nom. utsukAyate).
YEARNING (subs.): (1) spfhA (= longing);(2) vAtsalyam (= affection);(3) Otsukyam (= eager- -ness).
YEARNING , s. vatsalatA, vAtsalyaM, utsukatA, OtsukyaM, snehaH.
Yeast, s. surAmaMqaH, kArottaraH; kiRvaM, nagnahUH m.
YEAST: (1) surAmaRqaH;(2) kiRva (mn.);(3) aBizavaH.

YEAST , s. surAmaRqaH, madyamaRqaH, yavamaRqaH, kArottamaH, kArottaraH, kiRvaH -RvaM, nagnahUH -hu m. n., aBipavaH, kAdambarIvIjaM, surABAgaH. In some parts of India tAqI or tAlI, i. e. toddy or the fermented juice of the tāḍ or palm tree is much used as yeast.
YEEP: Bazati (Baz, c. 1.): v. To bark, cry.
Yell, v. i. A-ut-kruS 1 P, uccEH A-kraMd 1 P; See Scream. s. utkroSaH, cItkAraH, SabdaH, mahA-dIrGa-SabdaH.
To YELL , v. n. ru (c. 2. rOti, ravituM), ras, nad. See To SCREAM.
YELL , s. rutaM, rAvaH, dIrGarutaM, dIrGarAvaH, citkAraH. See SCREAM.
YELLING , part. dIrGarAvaH -vI -vaM, dIrGanAdI -dinI -di (n).
Yellow, a. pIta, pItala, haridrABa, gOra (rI f.), pItavarRa. [Yellow]ish, a. ApIta, haridrABa; ‘y(ellowish)-white’ pAMqura, ApAMqu. [Yellow]ness, s. pItavarRaH, pItatA.
YELLOW: (1) pIta (f. tA);(2) pItavarRa (f. rRA);(3) pItala (f. lA).
YELLOW , a. pItaH -tA -taM, gOraH -rI -raM, pItalaH -lA -laM, haridrABaH -BA -BaM, pItavarRaH -rRA -rRaM, gOravarRaH &c.
YELLOW-BIRD , YELLOW-HAMMER, s. haridrANgaH.
YELLOWISH: (1) ApIta (f. tA);(2) haridrABa (f. BA); etc.
YELLOWISH , a. IzatpItaH -tA -taM, IzatpItavarRaH -rRA -rRaM; ‘yellowish white,’ hariRaH -RA -RaM, pARquH -RquH -Rqu, pARquraH -rA -raM.
YELLOWNESS , s. pItatA, gOratA -tvaM, pItavarRaH, haridrAvarRaH.
To YELP , v. a. Baz, rE, ru, ras. See To BARK, YELL.
Yeoman, s. kzetrapAlaH, gfhapatiH; ‘y(eoman)ly service’ upayuktA-bahumAnanIyA-sevA.
YEOMAN: (1) gfhasTaH (?);(2) gfhapatiH (?);(3) kzetrapAlaH (?).
YEOMAN , s. gfhasTaH, gfhADikArI m. (n), kzetrapatiH m.
Yes, adv. bAQaM, AM, aTa kiM, taTA, evaM; evameva; sometimes by repeating verbs; ‘saying y(es)’ taTeti uktvA.

YES: (1) aTa kim, do the Rishis bear message from Kaṇva, y.: kiM kaRvasandeSahAriRastapasvinaH ? aTa kim, Sa. v.; y. by your favour my mercantile business is not failing: aTa kim, Aryasya prasAdena nAKaRqitA me vaRijyA, Mu. i.;(2) vAQam (= very well, indeed);(3) evam (= so, with eva = just so);(4) by repetition of verb, y., I have heard of him: asti, SrUyate, Sa. i.; y., you have guessed all right: samyagupalakzitaM BavatyA, Sa.
YES , adv. vAQaM, Am, hUm, satyaM, taTeti, paramaM, evaM, om, aTakiM, svIkftaM.
Yester, a. hyastana (nI f.), hyastya. Yesterday, adv. hyaH, pUrvedyuH; ‘of y(esterday)’ hyastana (nI f.). Yesternight, s. gatarAtriH. adv. atItAyAM rAtrO.
YESTER , a. hyastanaH -nI -naM, hyastyaH -styA -styaM, paryupitaH -tA -taM.
YESTERDAY: (1) hyas, of y.: hyastana (f. nI); (2) pUrvedyUH (= on the previous day);(3) kalyam (= day gone by as well as day coming).
YESTERDAY , s. hyas, pfrvvedyus, gatadivasaH, gatadinaM, kalpaM; ‘relating to yesterday,’ hyastanaH -nI -naM, hyastyaH -styA -styaM.
YESTERNIGHT: (1) gatarAtriH;(2) kalyarAtriH; and sim. comp. s.
YESTERNIGHT , s. gatarAtriH f., gatA rAtriH, gatA yAminI.

Yet, conj. taTApi (correl. of yadyapi), not ex. when y(et) comes after api (puzpavatyapi pavitrA). adv. adyApi, aDunApi, idAnImapi. 2 (With adjectives) by aDikaM, paraM in comp.; ‘y(et) more glorious’ atoDikataraM tejasvin.

YET: I Nevertheless:(1) taTApi, yet I am desirous of hearing: taTApi SuSrUzuraham, Si. i. 29.; (2) not expr., although it is infested with fierce animals, y. it is frequented by sages: krUra- sattvApi munijanasevitA, K.;(3) parantu (= but: q. v.).II Of time:(1) adyApi, I y. think of her: adyApi tAM cintayAmi, J.;(2) aDunApi, where y. in the rainy season: aDunApi yatra jalaDarasamaye, K.;(3) idAnImapi.III Further, over and above, y. blacker: aDikatarakfzRa (f. zRA); y. another reason: aparamapi kAraRam: y. a little longer: etadaDikaM kiyatkzaRam.
YET , conj. taTApi, parantu, api, kintu. See NEVERTHELESS.
YET , adv. (Over and above) aDikaM, paraM. — (Hitherto) adya yAvat, adyaparyyantaM, adyApi, see HITHERTO, STILL.
YEW: SAKowajAtIyavfkzaviSezaH.

Yield, v. t. pra-, dA 1 P, 3 U; ‘y(ield)ing fruits and flowers’ PalapuzpadA (BUH); pra-sU. 2, 4 A, utpad c., jan c. (janayati). 2 tyaj 1 P, ut-vi-sfj 6 P, hA 3 P. 3 pra-dA, vi-tF 1 P, (with loc.). v. i. vaSaM gam 1 P or yA-i 2 P, vaSIBU 1 P. 2 SaraRaM prapad 4 A or gam &c. 3 (to anotherʼs opinion) anu-man 4 A, nirbaMDaM-svAgrahaM-tyaj, anu-ruD 4 A; ‘y(ield) to a superior foe’ vEtasIM vfttiM ASri 1 U (R. iv. 35); ‘y(ield)ed to his prowess’ vikramaSAlinastasya vaSaM yayO; ‘does not y(ield) to Sachi in majestic splendour’ ojasvitayA na parihIyate SacyAH (V. 3). s. utpannaM, PalaM, lABaH [Yield]ing, a. Palada-prada-dAyin. 2 anuroDin, anuvartin, anukUla.

YIELD: I To produce: q. v.(1) sUte (sU, c. 2.), y. ed gems in mines, crops in fields and elephants in forests: KaniBiH suzuve ratnaM kzetraM SasyErvanE- rgajAn, R. xvii. 66.;(2) dadAti, pra- (dA, c. 3. give), y. ing every crop: sarvaSasyaprada (f. dA).II To give up, relinquish.II To concede, allow, permit: q. v.: anumanyate (man, c. 4.).
YIELD (v. i.): I To give way: q. v.: vaSaM gacCati (gam, c. 1.), eti (i, c. 2.); etc.II To comply with: anumanyate (man, c. 4.: with acc.).
YIELD (subs.): utpannam: v. Produce, fruit.

To YIELD , v. a. (Produce, bear) utpad (c. 10. -pAdayati -yituM), jan (c. 10. janayati -yituM), dA (c. 3. dadAti, dAtuM), pradA; ‘fruit,’ PalaM dA or pradA, Pal. — (Give, grant, concede) anudA, pradA, dA, vitF (c. 1. -tarati -rituM -rItuM), anujYA, protsf in caus., see To CON- CEDE. — (Deliver up, surrender) utsfj (c. 6. -sfjati -srazwuM), visfj, avasfj, tyaj (c. 1. tyajati, tyaktuM), hA, vihA.
To YIELD , v. n. vaSIBU, vaSaM gam or upagam. See To SUBMIT.
YIELDING , a. (Bearing fruit) PaladaH -dA -daM, PalapradaH &c., PalavAn -vatI -vat (t), Palan -lantI &c., PalotpAdakaH -kA -kaM. — (Com- pliant) anukUlaH -lA -laM, anuroDI -DinI &c., see COMPLIANT.
YOJANA , s. (A measure of distance, equal to five miles, or, according to some, to nine miles) yojanaM.

Yoke, s. yugaH-gaM, Dur f., (DurA in comp.); ‘fit for the y(oke)’ yugya, Durya, prAsaMgya; (fig.) ‘being under a foreign y(oke)’ paravaSatA, pArataMtryaM. 2 yugaM, yugalaM, yugmaM. 3 yoktf baMDanaM, AbaMDaH. v. t. yuj 10, yoktrayati (D.), saMgam c.; ‘y(ok)ed to an unfit husband’ ananurUpapatisaMgatA; ‘y(oke)-fellow’ sahacaraH (rI f.).
YOKE (subs.): I Lit.: yugaH, fit for y.: yugya (f. gyA), K. v. 49.II A pair: q. v.: yugam. III Fig.: yoktram: v. Bond.
YOKE (v.): (1) yojayati (yuj, c. 10.);(2) yoktrayati (nomi.).

YOKE , s. (For the necks of oxen) yugaH -gaM, prAsaNgaH, AbadDaH; ‘of a plough,’ kuSaH; ‘pin of the yoke,’ yugakIlaH -lakaH; ‘tie of it,’ yoktraM, yotraM, AbanDaH. — (Yoke or pair of oxen) goyugaM, gomiTunaM. — (Fit for the yoke) yugyaH -gyA -gyaM, prAsaNgyaH &c.
To YOKE , v. a. yuj (c. 7. yunakti, c. 10. yojayati -yituM), niyuj.
YOKE-FELLOW: sahacara (f. rI): v. Compa- -nion.
YOKE-FELLOW , s. sahacaraH, sahavarttI m. (n), sahaBAvI m.

YOKED , p. p. yuktaH -ktA -ktaM, niyuktaH &c., saMsaktayugaH -gA -gaM; ‘is yoked,’ yujyate; ‘a yoked animal,’ yugyaH, prAsaNgyaH, SAkawaH; [Page849-a+ 50] ‘having yoked the steeds,’ yuktaturaNgaH -NgA -NgaM.
Yokel, s. grAmyaH, grAmIRaH, jAnapadaH.
Yolk, s. aMqamaDyaM, peSIgarBaH.
YOLK , s. (Of an egg) aRqamaDyaM, aRqamaDyaBAgaH, aRqahfdayaM, aRqakusamaM, aRqamaDyasTaH pItaBAgaH.
Yon, Yonder, a. adas, idam, (pron. a.) puro dfSyamAna, nAtidUrasTa. adv. nAtidUraM-re, stokAMtare, agrataH.
YON, YONDER: expr. by adas, the y. waters of Pampā: amUni pampAsalilAni, R. xiii. 30. Y. (i. e. further on): amutra, K.
YON , YONDER, a. nAtidUrasTaH -sTA -sTaM, IzaddUrasTaH -sTA -sTaM.
YON , YONDER, adv. nAtidUre -ratas, IzaddUre -ratas.
Yore, (of) purA, pUrvaM; See Formerly.
YORE: of y.: purA: v. Formerly.
YORE , adv. (Of yore) purA, prAkkAle, prAk, purastAt.
You, yUyaM. Your, a. tvadIya, yuzmadIya, tAvaka-yOzmAka- (kI f.), yOzmAkIRa.
YOU: tvad, therefore you: sa tvam, R. ii. 45.; y. yourself: tvameva, Ku. v. 67. y. alone know yUyameva jAnITa, Sa. v. 25.

YOU , pron. (For thou, in the sing.) tvaM nom. sing. — (In the plur.) yUyaM nom. pl. (yuzmad); ‘of you,’ yuzmAkaM; ‘you two,’ yuvAM. The honorific pron. BavAn m. (t), is often used for ‘you,’ with the 3d pers. sing. of the verb.

Young, a. yuvan (yUnI-yuvati-tI f.), taruRa (RI f.), bAla (of trees &c. also); alpavayas, kOmAra (rI f.), aBinavavayaska; (of men) oft. ex. by dArakaH, kumAraH in comp.; ‘y(oung) sage’ munikumAraH-rakaH, fzidArakaH; ‘y(oung) warrior’ vIrapotaH, bAlavIraH, oft. by (s.) in comp.; See below; ‘y(oung) one’ SAvaH-vakaH, arBakaH, apatyaM, potaH-takaH, SiSuH, qiMBaH, pfTukaH; ‘y(oung) of an elephant’, ‘y(oung) elephant’ gajaSiSuH, kalaBaH. [Young]er, a. yavIyas, kanIyas, anujanman; ‘y(oung) brother or sister’ anujaH-jA, avarajaH-jA, anaMtarajaH-jA. Youngster, s. bawuH, arBakaH, kumArakaH, bAlaH. Youth, s. yOvanaM, tAruRyaM, pUrvaM-navaM-praTamaM-vayaH, kOmAraM-rakaM; ‘being in the prime or heyday of her y(outh)’ praTame vayasi vartamAnA, navayOvanA; (‘state of y(outh)’) yOvana-daSA-padavI, tAruRyAvasTA, yOvanakAlaH &c. 2 (Young man) yuvan m., taruRaH, bAlaH, kumAraH-rakaH, bAlajanaH, kiSoraH. [Youth]ful, a. taruRavayaska; by potaH, bAlaH, in comp. See (a.). [Youth]fulness, s. tAruRyaM.

YOUNG (adj.): (1) yuvan (f. tI), having a y. wife: yuvajAniH, B. v. 13.; y. camel: dAserayuvA, Si.; y. sugarcane: yuvekzuH, Bha.;(2) taruRa (f. RI), y. wife: taruRI BAryA, H.;(3) bAla (f. lA = very y. child); y. plant: bAlapAdapaH, Sa.
YOUNG (subs.): (1) SAvaH, -kaH;(2) arBaH, -kaH; (3) potaH, -kaH;(4) qimbaH, -kaH: v. Also child.

YOUNG , a. bAlaH -lA -laM, yuvA m., yuvatiH -tI f., yUnI f., yuva n. (n), taruRaH -RA -RaM, alpavayAH -yAH -yaH (s), alpavayaskaH -skA -skaM, aBi- navavayaskaH &c., bAliSaH -SA -SaM, kOmAraH -rI -raM, kiSoraH -rA -raM, aBi- navaH -vA -vaM, pratinavaH &c., vayasTaH -sTA -sTaM, vayaHsTaH &c.; ‘a young man,’ kumAraH, yuvajanaH, bAlajanaH, taruRaH, rUQavayAH m. (s); ‘young woman,’ taruRI, kumArI, kanyA, yuvatI, bAlA, navayOvanA; ‘a young bird,’ see YOUNG, s.

YOUNG , s. (Young one of any animal) SAvakaH, SiSuH m., potaH -takaH, apatyaM, pAkaH -kA, arBakaH, qimBaH, pfTukaH, praTukaH, varkaraH -rI, kuRakaH; ‘a young bird,’ pakziSAvakaH; ‘a young mouse,’ mUzi- kaSAvakaH; ‘a young elephant,’ gajaSiSuH m.; ‘a young deer,’ mfgapotakaH.
YOUNGER: (1) yavIyas (f. sI), y. sister: yavIyasI svasA, R. xvi. 85.;(2) kanIyas (f. sI), D. Ph.: y. brother, sister:(1) anuja (f. jA); (2) avaraja (f. jA);(3) antaraja (f. jA);(4) jaGanyaja (f. jA).

YOUNGER , a. kanIyAn -yasI -yaH (s), kanizWaH -zWA -zWaM, yavIyAn &c., yavizWaH &c., anujaH -jA -jaM, anujAtaH -tA -taM, anujanmA -nmA -nma (n), jaGanyajaH -jA -jaM, avarajaH &c., avaravayaskaH -skA -skaM, avaraH -rA -raM.
YOUNGEST: (1) kanizWa f. zWA;(2) yavizWa f. zWA; (3) jaGanya f. nyA (rare), although y., senior in virtues: jaGanyo'pi guRajyezWaH, Sca.
YOUNGSTER , s. kumArakaH, bAlajanaH, kiSoraH, vawuH. See LAD.
YOUR: (1) tvadIya (f. yA);(2) tAvaka (f. kI); (3) tAvakIna (f. nA);(4) yuzmadIya (f. yA); (5) yOzmAka (f. kI);(6) yOzmAkIna (f. nI).

YOUR , YOUR'S, pron. tava gen. sing., yuzmAkaM gen. pl. (yuzmad), BavataH gen. sing., BavatAM gen. pl. (Bavat), tvadIyaH -yA -yaM, BavadIyaH &c., BAvatkaH -tkA -tkaM, yOzmAkaH -kI -kaM, yOzmAkInaH -nA -naM.
YOURSELF , pron. (Reciprocally) AtmA m. (n); as, ‘blame yourself,’ AtmAnaM ninda; ‘for yourself,’ AtmArTaM. — (Emphati- cally) svayaM, svatas; ‘you yourself,’ sa tvaM, see SELF.

YOUTH: I The age:(1) yOvanam, seeking plea- sures in y.: yOvane vizayEziRAm, R. i. 8.; a girl in the prime of y.: navayOvanA, R. ix. 7.;(2) tAruRyam, exchange of y.: tAruRyavinimayaH, C. r.; (3) navaM vayas (n.), Ku. v. 41.;(4) praTamaM vayaH, K.II The state:(1) yOvanam, -daSA, H.;(2) tAruRyam, -avasTA.III A young man:(1) yuvan (m.), ascetic y.: tapoDanayuvA, K.;(2) taruRaH, y. s are fond of young women: taruRastAvattaruRIraktaH, J.; (3) yuvajanaH.

YOUTH , s. (Early part of life) yOvanaM, yOvanAvasTA, yOvanakAlaH, yOvanadaSA, kOmAraM, tAruRyaM, tAruRyadaSA, tAruRyakAlaH, sOkumAryyaM, SESavaM, praTamavayas n., pUrvvavayas n., pratyagravayas n., kESoraM; ‘prime or heyday of youth,’ navayOvanaM, yOvanaprOQiH f.; ‘pride of youth,’ yOvanadarpaH. — (A young man) taruRaH, kumAraH -rakaH, yuva- janaH, yuvA m. (n), bAlajanaH, abAlaH, kiSoraH, vawuH m., vawukaH, vekawaH. — (Young persons) taruRajanAH m. pl., yuvajanAH m. pl., bAlajanatA. — (State of being young) tAruRyaM, bAlatvaM -tA.
YOUTHFUL: (1) yOvanavat (f. tI);(2) taruRavayaska (f. skA); etc.: v. Also young.
YOUTHFUL , a. yOvanavAn -vatI -vat (t), bAlaH -lA -laM, yOvaneyakaH -kI -kaM, alpavayAH -yAH -yaH (s). See YOUNG.
YOUTHFULNESS: taruRavayaskatA and sim. comp. s: v. Youth.
YOUTHFULNESS , s. tAruRyaM, bAlatA -tvaM, sOkumAryyaM, bAliSyaM.
